config.title: useKeyPress

intro.title: useKeyPress
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom Vue composable called `useKeyPress` that detects when a specific keyboard key is pressed. You will learn how to use the `ref` and `onMounted`/`onUnmounted` lifecycle hooks from Vue to manage reactive state and event listeners. The core concept involves handling DOM events like `keydown` and `keyup` to track key states and clean up listeners properly. By the end, you'll have a reusable function that can be integrated into any Vue component to respond to keyboard input.
intro.usecase: The useKeyPress pattern is essential for creating keyboard-navigable interfaces that enhance user productivity and accessibility. In real applications, you'll find it powering keyboard shortcuts in dashboards (like pressing 'Escape' to close modals or 'Ctrl+S' to save forms), navigation controls in media players (spacebar for play/pause, arrow keys for seeking), and filter panels where users can press 'Enter' to apply selections or 'Tab' to cycle through options. Developers implement this pattern to build professional-grade interfaces that work seamlessly for both mouse and keyboard users, improving overall user experience and efficiency.

objectives: Implement a reactive key press state variable using Vue's ref
Construct an event handler function to update state based on keyboard events
Integrate the keydown and keyup event listeners with lifecycle hooks
Apply the useKeyPress composable in a Vue component template
Manipulate the DOM to display real-time key press feedback
Configure conditional rendering based on specific key press states
Bind the key press state to control UI element visibility

steps.title: Import Vue and ref
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the ref function from 'vue'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Vue and ref from the Vue package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing from a module
import { ref, computed } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue framework and ref function are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: Vue and ref are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported Vue and ref.

steps.feedbackWrong: Check your import statement. You need to import both Vue and ref from 'vue'.

steps.title: Create the useKeyPress composable function
steps.instruction: Create a function named useKeyPress that takes a key parameter.
steps.hint: Define a function that accepts one parameter. You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function.
steps.seedCode:
import { ref } from 'vue'

// Create the useKeyPress function here
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a function named useKeyPress that takes a key parameter.
successCriteria: A function named useKeyPress is defined and accepts a key parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the function is named exactly 'useKeyPress' and accepts a key parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function is not correctly defined. It should be named 'useKeyPress' and take a key parameter.

steps.title: Initialize reactive state for key pressed status
steps.instruction: Inside the useKeyPress function, create a reactive state variable named keyPressed using ref, initialized to false.
steps.hint: Use the ref function you imported earlier to create a reactive reference with an initial boolean value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating reactive state for a toggle
const isActive = ref(false)
steps.expectedOutcome: The useKeyPress function now contains a keyPressed reactive variable that will track whether the target key is currently pressed.
successCriteria: A keyPressed variable is declared using ref() and initialized to false inside the useKeyPress function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using ref() to create the reactive variable and initializing it to false.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the useKeyPress function, create a reactive variable named keyPressed using ref(false).

steps.title: Define key up handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the useKeyPress function, define a handleKeyUp function that sets keyPressed to false when event.key matches the provided key parameter.
steps.hint: Create a function that takes an event parameter and checks if event.key equals the key parameter passed to useKeyPress. If they match, set keyPressed.value to false.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useKeyPress function now has a handleKeyUp function that will update the reactive state when the target key is released.
successCriteria: A handleKeyUp function is defined inside useKeyPress that sets keyPressed.value to false when event.key matches the key parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it properly checks if event.key matches the key parameter and sets keyPressed.value to false.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleKeyUp function is missing or doesn't properly update the keyPressed state when the key is released.

steps.title: Set up event listeners in onMounted
steps.instruction: Inside the useKeyPress function, import onMounted from 'vue' and use it to add event listeners for 'keydown' and 'keyup' events that call the handler functions.
steps.hint: Import onMounted from vue, then call onMounted with a callback function that adds event listeners to the window object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useKeyPress function will have onMounted imported and used to set up event listeners when the component mounts.
successCriteria: onMounted is imported from 'vue' and used inside useKeyPress to add event listeners for 'keydown' and 'keyup' events.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've imported onMounted and added both 'keydown' and 'keyup' event listeners inside the onMounted callback.
steps.feedbackWrong: The event listeners aren't set up correctly. Remember to import onMounted from 'vue' and use it to add both 'keydown' and 'keyup' event listeners to the window.

steps.title: Return the keyPressed state from composable
steps.instruction: At the end of the useKeyPress function, return the keyPressed reactive state so it can be used by components.
steps.hint: Make sure you return the keyPressed ref from the function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useKeyPress function now returns the keyPressed reactive state, making it available to components that use this composable.
successCriteria: The useKeyPress function returns the keyPressed ref.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning the keyPressed ref from the useKeyPress function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The composable should return the keyPressed reactive state. Add a return statement with keyPressed at the end of the function.

steps.title: Create main component and use the composable
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named KeyPressDemo that calls useKeyPress with the 'Enter' key and stores the returned value in a variable.
steps.hint: Define a component function that uses the useKeyPress composable you created earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: A component function named KeyPressDemo is created that calls useKeyPress('Enter') and stores the result.
successCriteria: The KeyPressDemo component is defined and calls useKeyPress('Enter'), storing the returned value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but make sure it calls useKeyPress('Enter') and stores the returned value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Create a function named KeyPressDemo that calls useKeyPress('Enter').

steps.title: Display key press status in template
steps.instruction: In the KeyPressDemo component's template, add a paragraph that displays whether the Enter key is currently pressed based on the keyPressed state returned from useKeyPress.
steps.hint: Use the keyPressed ref value in a template expression to show 'Enter key is pressed' or 'Enter key is not pressed'.

steps.expectedOutcome: The component will display a paragraph showing the current status of the Enter key press.
successCriteria: A paragraph element exists in the template that displays 'Enter key is pressed' when keyPressed is true and 'Enter key is not pressed' when false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a paragraph, but it might not be correctly displaying the key press status. Make sure you're using the keyPressed value from the composable and showing appropriate text for both true and false states.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph displaying key press status is missing or incorrect. Check that you've added a paragraph element in the template that shows whether the Enter key is pressed based on the keyPressed state.
